summary: Update Slack automation for Support bridges: create bridge channel, pin SUP ticket, and post escalation template
content:
Owner: Benji Okafor (Platform automation)
Support Ops: Dev Patel
SRE partner: Rafael Mendes

Background
Support is standardizing how we start Slack bridges during customer escalations. Today bridge creation and context sharing is inconsistent (missing request IDs, region, model, and SUP link), and follow-ups are hard to find after the bridge ends. This task updates Slack automation so the first 2–3 minutes of an escalation are predictable and match the new playbook.

Goal
When Support creates a bridge channel for an escalation, Slack automation should:
1) Create a correctly named bridge channel (or validate naming),
2) Prompt for required escalation context (tier, severity/P-level, region, model, request IDs, symptom, start time),
3) Post the approved escalation template message (customer-safe),
4) Prompt for the related SUP ticket key and pin it (and optionally pin the template message),
5) Provide a one-click action to move/escalate to #incidents when triggers are met, without bypassing SRE process.

Scope
- Slack Workflow/shortcut to create a Support bridge channel from #support.
- Auto-post “Escalation Template” message in the new bridge channel.
- Prompt user for SUP key and post + pin the Jira issue link.
- Optionally prompt to add participants (Support on-call, SRE on-call, Platform on-call) using the contact list from the escalation playbook.
- Ensure the workflow does not leak customer-sensitive details into #announcements or broadly visible channels.

Out of scope
- Replacing #incidents process or building a full incident-management system in Slack.
- Auto-creating Jira tickets (handled by Support workflow; automation should link/pin only).

Requirements (from playbook)
- Channel naming convention (per Confluence):
  - Support bridge: "sup-bridge-<SUPKEY>-<short-topic>" (example: sup-bridge-SUP-1842-streaming-resets)
  - If severity escalates to an incident: move to #incidents per SRE guidance and use incident channel naming there.
- Required context at creation:
  - Customer tier, priority (P0–P4), severity (Sev0–Sev3 if applicable)
  - Environment + region(s)
  - Model + endpoint (chat/embeddings/rerank)
  - Example request IDs / timestamps
  - Symptom summary and current customer impact
- The bridge must link the SUP ticket and keep it discoverable after the bridge ends.

Proposed implementation
A) Slack Workflow Builder shortcut (preferred for speed)
- Shortcut name: "Start Support Bridge"
- Trigger location: #support and #customer-success (restricted to Support/CS user groups)
- Form fields:
  - SUP key (required; validation message: “Use SUP-#### format”)
  - Customer tier (dropdown)
  - Priority (dropdown P0–P4)
  - Severity (dropdown Sev0–Sev3; optional unless P0/P1)
  - Region(s) (free text)
  - Model(s) (free text)
  - Endpoint (dropdown)
  - Request IDs (free text)
  - Start time (optional)
  - One-line symptom (required)
- Workflow step: Create channel named "sup-bridge-${SUPKEY}-${short_topic}" (if Slack limitations prevent templated name, create channel with SUP key then prompt rename and post an instruction block)
- Workflow step: Post template (see below) and pin it
- Workflow step: Post Jira link for SUP key and pin it
- Workflow step: Post “Next actions” block with:
  - Links to severity matrix + escalation triggers
  - Link to Support intake checklist
  - Reminder: if triggers met, move to #incidents and page SRE per escalation paths

B) Integration with incident-bot (ENG-4830 / PR-209)
- Ensure incident-bot prompts for SUP keys in #incidents channels and pins them.
- Ensure Support bridge workflow does not duplicate incident-bot behavior in #incidents; it should hand off cleanly.

Escalation template (customer-safe)
Header: "Support Bridge — Escalation Context"
Fields:
- SUP ticket: <link>
- Customer tier:
- Priority / Severity:
- Environment / Region(s):
- Model(s) / Endpoint:
- Symptom:
- Start time / first observed:
- Example request IDs / timestamps:
- Current impact (how many customers/requests, revenue risk if known):
- Recent deploys / config changes (if known):
- What we’ve tried:
- What we need from Eng/SRE:
- Owner (Support):
- Owner (Eng/SRE):

Acceptance criteria
- From #support, a Support agent can run a single shortcut and get a new bridge channel with the template posted and pinned.
- SUP ticket link is posted and pinned within the bridge channel.
- Workflow prompts for minimum required fields (SUP key + symptom + region), and strongly nudges for request IDs.
- Workflow output aligns with Confluence “Slack bridge conventions” and does not include customer-specific confidential artifacts by default.
- Handoff to #incidents is clear; workflow includes a “when to move to #incidents” reminder and links to triggers.

Testing plan
- Dry run using SUP-1842 (streaming resets) and SUP-1850 (eu-west embeddings timeouts) to validate template usability.
- Validate pin permissions and channel creation permissions for Support On-Call user group.
- Verify link formatting and channel naming length constraints.

Risks / notes
- Slack channel name length + character constraints may require truncating <short-topic>.
- If Slack Workflow Builder cannot dynamically create channel names as needed, we may need a lightweight internal app/bot step.
- Must ensure the shortcut is restricted; bridge channels can include sensitive operational details.

Rollout
- Target: end of known-issues sprint follow-up week (adoption/cleanup).
- Announce in #support and #announcements with a 1-minute how-to + link to playbook.
- Update Support onboarding snippet library to reference the shortcut.
comments: 2026-02-10 (Dev Patel): Creating INT-332 to track the Slack workflow updates discussed in the playbook refresh. Biggest pain: bridges start without request IDs + no pinned SUP link, so Eng loses context when it scrolls. Please align with the Confluence Slack bridge conventions page and Rafael’s feedback on required context.

2026-02-11 (Rafael Mendes): +1. Required fields for pages/bridges: request IDs, region, model, endpoint, and “what changed recently” if known. Also: do not encourage bypassing #incidents; we need a clear reminder of when to move it. Happy to review the template copy.

2026-02-12 (Benji Okafor): I can do a Workflow Builder first pass. Open question: channel naming—Slack workflows can create channels but dynamic naming is limited. If we can’t reliably name with the SUP key, we’ll create a channel then post an instruction + quick rename guidance. Will report back after a prototype.

2026-02-13 (Dylan Brooks): For INT-333 I’m adding Jira required-field enforcement and SLA reminders. If you can ensure the workflow collects SUP key + region + priority, I can mirror those as Jira required fields at triage for consistency.

2026-02-14 (Benji Okafor): Prototype built in staging workspace: shortcut posts template + pins template. Still need SUP key prompt → Jira link + pin. Also added links to severity matrix + intake checklist. Need approval from Support Ops on final wording before enabling in prod.

2026-02-16 (Elliot Price): Please keep the template customer-safe and avoid default prompts that encourage copying logs into Slack. Suggest adding: “Share only request IDs and timestamps; attach logs in Jira if needed.” I’ll review the final message block.

2026-02-18 (Benji Okafor): Implemented SUP key prompt and Jira link pinning. Next step is permissions + restricting the shortcut to Support/CS user groups. Pending: final copy review from Dev + Rafael, then enable in prod and post announcement.
